correctness.rationale: For each forest F, all homomorphisms into an n-vertex d-regular G count as n^components d^edges. Induction over image-kernel quotients and girth excluding cyclic quotients proves universal injective forest embeddings for every edge count below girth. A multinomial expansion of the Gaussian absolute edge-difference sum then gives universal raw moments. Exact chi normalization converts these to intrinsic spherical width moments. The volume comparison follows from the matrix-tree and zonotope determinant-sum identities; exact integer BFS, forest-shape census and Bareiss Laplacian determinants are replayed from the packaged verify.py. Finite tests only support the example; the infinite-family statement is proved analytically.

value.rationale: All-orders-below-girth exact Euclidean-width moment universality has a natural graph-geometric motivation, beyond routine third-moment substitution. The explicit same-dimension cubic 20-vertex pair has equal first four width moments but different exact Euclidean volumes by 32/27, showing a substantial and surprising nonreconstructibility of volume from low-order random projections. It is a structural infinite-family theorem with an independently reproducible noncongruent witness, not an arbitrary finite computation.
